correctness.rationale: For the larger L-stable ROS2 parameter, the stability function reduces to a rational function with a single repeated pole. Its kth derivative has one affine sign factor, \(1+\sqrt2-k+(3+2\sqrt2)h\). On \(J_n=-I+N_n\), nilpotency makes the exact matrix function a finite Taylor series whose kth coefficient occupies a distinct subdiagonal. Entrywise positivity is therefore equivalent to nonnegativity of all derivatives through order \(n-1\), and monotonicity in k reduces the test sharply to the highest order. The packaged checker independently replays the threshold algebra and the exact four-state sign witness.

originality.rationale: The original ROS2 report proves scalar stability-function positivity and motivates it for stiff chemistry, but it does not address matrix positivity on coupled Metzler systems. The later monotonicity paper observes positivity of the stability function and its first two derivatives and a third-derivative obstruction, but stops at weak absolute monotonicity and does not derive a state-count phase law. Targeted searches found no source converting those derivative facts into the exact serial-chain threshold \(n\le2+\sqrt2+(3+2\sqrt2)h\).

value.rationale: ROS2 was designed for stiff atmospheric chemistry where nonnegative species concentrations are physically essential. Serial irreversible transfer and decay chains are a natural linear subsystem class. The theorem turns a qualitative weak-absolute-monotonicity observation into a complete sharp safety map: dimensions up to three are unconditionally safe, dimension four is the first failure, and every longer chain has an exact lower recovery threshold. The counterintuitive fact that decreasing a positive step can create negativity while increasing it restores positivity is directly relevant to interpreting step-size safeguards for stiff positive systems.
